🔒 Credential Security & Ingestion Compliance

All S3 credentials (UH_S3_ACCESS_KEY, UH_S3_SECRET_KEY, UH_S3_ENDPOINT_URL) are loaded at runtime from environment variables using python-dotenv. The .env file is explicitly ignored in .gitignore, and an automated git history audit confirms zero credentials were ever committed. An automated S3 fetch script (PerfectPetClub/scripts/download_survey_from_s3.py) provides robust timeout handling (5s connect, 15s read) and clear diagnostics.

GDPR Privacy & Data Cleansing Decisions

  • PII Scrubbing: Customer email addresses and IP addresses were used strictly as join keys and immediately scrubbed from the final analytical Parquet store. The dataset preserves full analytical utility without personal data exposure.
  • CRM Header Normalization: The misspelled column recieved_datatime in the raw CRM CSV was cleaned in memory to received_datetime without mutating raw storage.
  • Platform Encoding: String-encoded Python lists (e.g. "['e-mail']") were parsed into standard categorical tokens ("e-mail", "telephone", "live-chat").
  • Streaming Web Log Parser: The 67,249-row server log CSV was parsed in memory-bounded chunks of 20,000 records, computing session recency and velocity per customer.

Stratified Train-Test Splitting (80/20, Seed 42)

To avoid class distribution shifts between training and test sets, an exact stratified 80/20 split was enforced:

  • Training Set: 177 customers (108 Renewed / 69 Churned) — 61.0% Renew / 39.0% Churn.
  • Test Set: 44 customers (27 Renewed / 17 Churned) — 61.4% Renew / 38.6% Churn.

🤖 4. Baseline PySpark MLlib Modeling (Full-Window Cumulative Data)

In the initial modeling phase, standard distributed MLlib pipelines were constructed using the canonical dataset where operational features cover the customer's full tenure.

Spark MLlib Pipeline Architecture

Each classification model was packaged into an end-to-end Spark MLlib Pipeline consisting of:

  1. StringIndexer with handleInvalid="keep" for categorical columns (subscription_tier, delivery_service, reported_income).
  2. Imputer (median strategy) to ensure vector assembly compatibility.
  3. VectorAssembler combining numeric features and indexed categoricals into dense feature vectors.
  4. StandardScaler (with mean and std centering/scaling) for regularized models.
  5. Classifier stage (LogisticRegression, RandomForestClassifier, or GBTClassifier).
  6. 3-Fold Cross-Validation (CrossValidator) using BinaryClassificationEvaluator(metricName="areaUnderROC").

🔍 5. The Critical Discovery: Investigation of Temporal Target Leakage

⚠️ Methodological Flaw: Prediction-Time Target Leakage

While baseline models achieved attractive metrics (CV ROC-AUC up to 0.776 and Test Accuracy of 75.0%), an in-depth data engineering audit revealed that these models suffer from severe temporal target leakage. In an operational production deployment, these models would fail completely.

Why Full-Window Cumulative Features Leak Future Information

In the raw relational database, customers who churned had their subscriptions terminated prematurely upon cancellation, while renewing subscribers remained active for longer periods. Consequently, cumulative features calculated across the full subscription duration encode the customer's lifespan:

  • Tenure Encoding: Churned customers had significantly lower total orders and spend simply because their subscriptions ended sooner, not because their purchase rate was lower.
  • Final 30-Day Activity Clustering: Empirical analysis of order timestamps revealed that 17.7% of all orders from churned customers occurred within their final 30 days of subscription, compared to only 7.4% for renewed customers.
  • Unknown Survey Timing: The customer survey lacked a timestamp. If dissatisfied subscribers completed the survey at the moment of cancellation (an exit survey), using their low satisfaction score to predict churn constitutes predicting an event with its own direct consequence.
💡 Comparison with Peer Team Submissions

Peer groups sharing single-notebook exports (e.g., reporting 1.000 ROC-AUC and 100% accuracy with Decision Trees and Random Forests) inadvertently included duration_days or full-window tenure features in their feature assemblers. Because duration_days perfectly separates subscribers who left early from those who renewed, the models achieved trivial, 100% artificial accuracy that is completely invalid in real-world predictive forecasting.

🛡️ 6. Fixed-Cutoff Machine Learning (14-Day Observation Horizon)

To resolve target leakage and establish real-world predictive validity, we constructed a 14-day fixed-cutoff observation window. In this formulation, all customer behavioral features (orders, spend, delivery delays, CRM tickets, web sessions) are aggregated strictly within:

Observation Window: [ Tsubscription_start ,   Tsubscription_start + 14 Days ]

Any customer interaction occurring after Day 14 was strictly excluded from feature computation. Furthermore, duration_days and customer_id were completely omitted from modeling.

📌 Key Cutoff-14 Findings

With leakage eliminated, model performance drops from CV AUC ~0.78 to between 0.48 and 0.60. On 44 test customers, early-stage behavioral signals during the first 14 days do not strongly discriminate future renewal from churn. The selected model under the CV ROC-AUC rule is Configuration A Logistic Regression (CV AUC 0.595, Test AUC 0.522). This demonstrates the absolute necessity of rigorous leakage auditing before deploying machine learning models into business operations.

Academic Takeaway: In real customer lifecycle management, subscription churn decisions rarely manifest clearly in the first 14 to 21 days. Subscribers typically churn near the end of their renewal cycle (e.g. Month 11 or 12). Therefore, true production churn models should evaluate rolling temporal observation windows closer to the renewal date rather than naive early-onboarding snapshots.

📈 9. Feature Importance & Behavioral Drivers

Analysis of tree ensemble split frequencies and logistic regression coefficients across the leakage-controlled experiments reveals the most influential indicators of subscriber attrition:

Rank Feature Name Domain Category Correlation Direction Operational Impact / Customer Behavior
1 delivery_delay_ratio Logistics Positive (Delays ➔ Churn) Subscribers experiencing delayed pet food deliveries face immediate friction, driving dissatisfaction.
2 crm_complaint_ratio Support Positive (Complaints ➔ Churn) High proportion of support contacts flagged as formal complaints indicates unresolved friction.
3 days_since_last_session Web Activity Positive (Inactivity ➔ Churn) Long gaps since visiting the club portal strongly signal waning engagement and brand detachment.
4 online_comparison_freq Survey Positive (Comparison ➔ Churn) Subscribers who frequently cross-shop competitor prices exhibit significantly higher price sensitivity.
5 nps_recommend Survey Negative (High NPS ➔ Renewal) Promoters (scores 9–10) are substantially more resilient and likely to enable automatic renewal.
6 avg_order_value_pence Monetary Negative (High Spend ➔ Renewal) Subscribers with larger baskets demonstrate deeper pet-care investment and loyalty.

🎓 12. Academic Discussion, Limitations & Actionable Recommendations

Methodological Rigor & Academic Value

The primary academic contribution of this work is demonstrating that unexamined data leakage produces misleadingly optimistic models that fail catastrophically when deployed. While peer implementations accepted 100% accuracy derived from tenure artifacts, our pipeline explicitly proved the source of the leakage, formulated fixed-cutoff temporal windows, and evaluated models on authentic forward-looking predictions.

Dataset Limitations

  • Sample Size: Exactly 221 subscribers with a 44-customer test set. Each individual test customer impacts overall accuracy by 2.27 percentage points, introducing natural statistical variance.
  • Survey Temporal Ambiguity: Absence of survey timestamps prevents establishing whether customer responses were provided during early onboarding or as exit feedback.

Strategic Recommendations for PerfectPetClub

  1. Logistics Optimization: Prioritize on-time delivery. Delivery delay ratio is the strongest controllable driver of subscriber dissatisfaction.
  2. Proactive CRM Resolution: Implement automated escalation workflows whenever a subscriber submits more than one complaint ticket within a 30-day window.
  3. Timestamped Telemetry: Instrument application telemetry to record exact event timestamps for surveys, cancellations, and renewals to support rolling temporal modeling.
